subject: Ceres5B 503 spike — customer communication and recovery steps
messages:
From: Julia Reed <julia.reed@acme-retail.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@acme-retail.com
Date: 2027-03-03T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 503s from Ceres5B in production

Hi Karthik,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 503 responses from the /generate endpoint this morning around 08:50 PT. The failures are concentrated on requests routed to model Ceres5B (we have model pinned in our integration). The errors are impacting checkout chat suggestions — roughly 12% of calls are returning 503s.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is a platform incident or something on our integration/config? We need an ETA for resolution; impact is hitting customer-facing flows.

Thanks,
Julia
Julia Reed
Product Ops — Acme Retail

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T15:20:00Z
Subject: Re: sudden 503s from Ceres5B in production

Hi Julia — thanks for the heads up and the sample. We’re seeing the same spike on our side and have opened an incident (INC-4589). I’ve looped in our on-call infra and model ops teams. Immediate notes: 1) spike began ~08:45 PT, 2) primarily observed on Ceres5B on us-west-2, 3) error signature matches model-level runtime 503s rather than network gateway failures.

Short next steps: I’ll share a short status update in 30 mins. For now please keep traffic steady if possible (we want to collect logs), and we’ll advise if you should switch to the fallback model ID.

Apologies for the disruption — working on this as priority.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0132

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T15:34:00Z
Subject: RE: sudden 503s from Ceres5B in production

Karthik / team — quick internal update from infra/model-ops: we observed a correlated increase in per-shard queue saturation on Ceres5B instances in us-west-2. Initial hypothesis: a kernel-level memmove regression in the optimized attention kernel under a specific sequence-length mix causing slowdowns and eventual request rejections (503).

What we’ve done so far:
- Rolled a temporary kernel fallback on a subset of nodes (20%) which reduced 503 rate for that cohort to ~1.5%.
- Enabled request-level hedging for affected routes (short-term) to reduce user-facing error rate.
- Collected diagnostic traces and payload samples; attached a short log excerpt.

Recommended customer-facing messaging: apology, brief explanation that this is a model-serving performance regression affecting Ceres5B on us-west-2, a note that we have mitigation (kernel fallback & hedging) in place, and an ETA of 2–4 hours for full roll-forward to stable nodes.

I’ll coordinate with SRE to push the fallback to 60% in the next 30 minutes if error rates don’t drop further.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: ceres5b-diagnostics-0303.pdf]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Julia Reed <julia.reed@acme-retail.com>, support@acme-retail.com
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-04T02:42:00Z
Subject: Update: Ceres5B 503 spike — mitigation and recovery confirmed

Hi Julia — quick update and apology for the disruption. Our mitigation actions (kernel fallback + hedging + rolling stable nodes) reduced the global 503 rate from ~12% to under 0.5% for your tenant. We completed the roll-forward to stable nodes in us-west-2 at 01:35 PT and have observed normal error rates since then.

What we did:
- Identified a regression in an optimized attention kernel under specific request mix.
- Applied kernel fallback across affected nodes and hedging on impacted routes.
- Rolled stable node set and validated end-to-end request success rates.

Recommended action for your integration: no change required. If you prefer, we can switch your routing to the fallback model variant for 24 hours while we complete the postmortem and a full kernel patch.

We’ll follow up with a technical postmortem tomorrow that includes root cause, timeline, and corrective fixes. I’m sorry again for the impact — we know these interruptions are costly and appreciate your patience.

If you’d like a short post-incident call, I’m available today at 17:00 PT.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
